images.title: Loch Long at Arrochar by Ian S, CC BY-SA 2.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Loch Long at Arrochar. The Sea Loch extends from the Firth of Clyde at its southwestern end. It measures approximately 20 miles in length. The loch also has an arm, Loch Goil, on its western side. Loch Long forms part of the coast of the Cowal peninsula and forms the entire western coastline of the Rosneath Peninsula.

images.title: Gareloch View by Mary and Angus Hogg, CC BY-SA 2.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Gareloch View. An open sea loch in Argyll and Bute. The loch is well used for recreational boating, water sports and fishing. Harbour and grey seals are often seen in the Gare Loch along with pods of porpoise. Bottle Nose whales were photographed in September 2020

description: This super route is suitable for both walkers and mountain bikers. It runs from Balloch to Inveruglas passing Loch Lomond (see video), The Gareloch, Arrochar, Loch Long and Loch Sloy. There's some stunning mountainous scenery and splendid views of the Firth of Clyde as you pass through this beautiful area.

details.subtitle: Pubs/Cafes
details.content: In Helensburgh the Commodore is a nice place for a pit stop on the walk. The main draw is a great outdoor seating area with views over the Firth of Clyde. They also serve good quality food and have a fine selection of drinks. You can find them at 112-117 W Clyde St, G84 8ES.

details.subtitle: Further Information and Other Local Ideas
details.content: At Loch Lomond you can explore the lovely Balloch Castle Country Park and pick up the West Lomond Cycle Path which takes you along the western side of the loch. For more walking ideas in the area see the Loch Lomond and the Trossachs Walks page.
